facts.statement: Resources are technologically accessible, economically feasible, and culturally acceptable elements of the environment.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.1

facts.statement: Individual, Community, National, and International resources form the classification based on ownership.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.2

facts.statement: Oceanic resources up to 12 nautical miles ($22.2\ \text{km}$) from the coast are termed territorial waters and belong to the nation.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.2

facts.statement: The oceanic resources beyond 200 nautical miles of the Exclusive Economic Zone belong to open ocean and no individual country can utilise them without international concurrence.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.2

facts.statement: Sustainable development means development should take place without damaging the environment and without compromising the needs of future generations.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.3

facts.statement: The first international Earth Summit was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil in June 1992, endorsing Agenda 21.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.3

facts.statement: Black soil is also known as regur soil and is ideal for growing cotton ('black cotton soil').
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.6

facts.statement: Black soil is rich in calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime, but generally poor in phosphoric content.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.6

facts.statement: Alluvial soil is deposited by three important Himalayan river systems: Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.6

facts.statement: Old alluvial soil is called Bangar (higher concentration of kankar nodules) and new alluvial soil is called Khadar (more fertile).
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.6

facts.statement: Laterite soil develops in areas with high temperature and heavy rainfall, resulting in intense leaching.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.6

facts.statement: Red soil develops a reddish color due to diffusion of iron in crystalline and metamorphic rocks.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.6

facts.statement: Gully erosion occurs when running water cuts through clayey soils making deep channels, creating badland topography in the Chambal basin.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.7

facts.statement: Sheet erosion takes place when water flows as a sheet over large areas down a slope and washes away the topsoil.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.7

facts.statement: Planting lines of trees to create shelter (shelter belts) stabilizes sand dunes in western India.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.7

facts.statement: The National Forest Policy of India (1952) outlined 33% of geographical area should be under forest cover for ecological balance.
facts.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.4

definitions.definition: Total area sown with crops and orchards, counted once in a particular year.
definitions.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.4

definitions.definition: Area sown more than once in an agricultural year plus net sown area.
definitions.source: NCERT Class 10 SST Geography Ch 1 Section 1.4

common_misconceptions.misconception: Students swap Khadar and Bangar soils
common_misconceptions.truth: Khadar is the newer, more fertile low-lying river alluvium; Bangar is the older, less fertile terrace alluvium with kankar.
common_misconceptions.source: CBSE Class 10 Social Science Marking Scheme 2023 Q18

board_exam_questions.question: Which one of the following soils is ideal for growing cotton?
board_exam_questions.explanation: Regur soil (black soil) has high clay content and moisture retention, making it ideal for cotton cultivation.
board_exam_questions.source: CBSE Class 10 Board Exam 2023 Set 1 Q1

mcqs.question: Which soil is also known as 'Regur' soil?
mcqs.explanation: Black soil of the Deccan trap is known locally as Regur soil.

mcqs.question: In which city was the first international Earth Summit held in 1992?
mcqs.explanation: The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED) met at Rio de Janeiro, Brazil in June 1992.

mcqs.question: Territorial water extends up to what distance from the baseline coast of a nation?
mcqs.explanation: Oceanic resources up to 12 nautical miles ($22.2\ \text{km}$) belong to the nation as territorial waters.

mcqs.question: What is the new alluvial soil deposited by floods every year called?
mcqs.explanation: Khadar is the newer, fine-textured alluvium renewed every annual flood.

mcqs.question: Which of the following states suffers predominantly from land degradation due to over-irrigation?
mcqs.explanation: Over-irrigation in Punjab and Haryana causes waterlogging, leading to increased salinity and alkalinity in the soil.

mcqs.question: What percentage of geographical area was targeted for forest cover in India's National Forest Policy (1952)?
mcqs.explanation: The 1952 National Forest Policy stipulated 33% forest cover for maintaining ecological balance.

mcqs.question: Deep ravines and badland topography caused by gully erosion are particularly famous in which basin?
mcqs.explanation: The Chambal ravines in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan are classic examples of severe gully erosion badlands.

mcqs.question: Laterite soil is formed due to which of the following natural processes?
options: Intense leaching under high temperature and heavy rainfall
mcqs.answer: Intense leaching under high temperature and heavy rainfall
mcqs.explanation: Laterite develops under high temperature and heavy rainfall where tropical downpours wash away soluble nutrients.

mcqs.question: Planting shelter belts of trees is an effective method to control soil erosion in which region?
mcqs.explanation: Shelter belts break wind velocity and stabilize shifting sand dunes in dry desert regions of Rajasthan.

mcqs.question: Why is red soil reddish in appearance?
options: Diffusion of iron in crystalline and metamorphic rocks
mcqs.answer: Diffusion of iron in crystalline and metamorphic rocks
mcqs.explanation: Iron diffusion in ancient crystalline rocks gives red soil its reddish hue; it looks yellow when hydrated.
